claims.COMMENTS: bare() reads a node as written: its tokens' own text in order, the trivia between two tokens kept as written when it is white space alone, in a node a comment walks too (C-LINES). A trivia run that holds a comment - a block, a line or a JSDoc-style comment, a JSDoc comment the parser attaches as a node too (its node is no token: M-JSDOC) - is read whole, its white space, line ends, blank and white-space-only lines with it: as nothing right after a token whose text ends in a terminator (the '.', '...', ';', '?.', '!', '?' and '??' punctuators and a number written with a trailing '.'), so the reading reads on uncut there (T-R1, T-R3, T-TOKENS, M-AFTER); and as one space anywhere else (T-R1C, M-BEFORE), where a line boundary the run holds cuts nothing either - a subject and a family across it find (U-OWN-LINE, U-BLANK) and a marker across it quiets the reading, which LIVE QUIET holds (U-MARKER). So no comment cuts an as-written reading, a marker in a comment quiets nothing (M-AFTER, M-BEFORE) and a family word in a comment finds nothing (M-WORDS).
claims.AS-WRITTEN: The as-written readings are the 13 sites bare() reads: a property access, a qualified name, an element access's receiver, an indexed access type's object type, an object binding pattern's receiver (a variable's initializer, a for-of's and a for-in's iterated expression, a parameter's type annotation and its default value), a destructuring assignment's receiver (the assigned expression, a for-of's and a for-in's iterated expression) and an import-equals entity name - each read with every comment kind right after a '.' inside it (M-AFTER) and before that '.' or inside its brackets (M-BEFORE), one finding each.
claims.CUT: SENTENCES cuts an as-written reading where its text holds a boundary as written: white space alone - a space or a line end - right after a token that ends in a terminator (C-SPACE), a blank or white-space-only line, a line read as a table row, a heading or a list item (a '-', '+' or '*' bullet, or a number with ')'; a number with '.' is a terminator cut, C-SPACE), or a terminator before white space inside a string, a template, a regular expression or JSX text the reading holds (C-LINES). A subject and a family on two sides of a cut read no finding while the uncut twin finds once, every cut member is held by LIVE QUIET (fail closed: the residual R-CUT), and a cut can part a marker away, which then finds (C-OVER-READ).
claims.LIVE QUIET: quietOf holds, beside the quiet readings of one text, every carrier pair whose two words a sentence cut parts - each occurrence of each pair, in a code reading and across a page's sentences - as '<where> parted:carrier <pair>' (P-ONE, P-C04, P-C05, P-C06, P-CODE); a pair one sentence spells is a finding and is held as parted nowhere, while a parted occurrence of the same pair beside it is held (P-WITHIN).
